newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan oil firms say Super Light no longer needed.
newsitem.headline: Japan oil firms say Super Light no longer needed.

text.p: Several Japanese oil firms said on Monday that they had dropped term purchases of Arab Super Light (ASL) crude because they now had facilities which made it unnecessary for them to purchase the extra light crude.
One of the few exception is Taiyo Oil Co Ltd which renewed contract volumes for ASL last year when contracts came up for review with state-owned Saudi Aramco.
"(Arab Super Light) became a crude grade that we didn't need to buy any longer," a trader with an oil company said.
Japanese traders said that many oil companies were now equipped with secondary processing equipment.
This means that they no longer need to depend on the high quality crude to produce more light products.
Taiyo Oil, however, does not have the upgrading facility and it continues to lift about 20,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) of the crude.
ASL is lifted from a port on the Red Sea which also makes it operationally more complicated for Japanese firms, the trader with the oil company also said.
ASL exports to the Far East for October lifting are priced at a $2.40 a barrel premium to the regional price markers of Oman and Dubai crude.
